answer: A wharf charges berthing by the night, so squatters cannot linger. Each identity must secure a berth countersigned by two holders outside its own dune, and one berth backs one identity, so n aliases need n separate signers rather than one crew. Berthing is priced by rank: the k-th berth an operator claims costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. Every claim is carved into a shared glacier ledger, and an audit re-walks a random berth; an unconfirmed claim melts the whole shelf and forfeits its bonds.
